title: Godot 2D workflow - Summer Engine or OpenCode Go?
author: LiveCourage334
selftext:
I have been playing with both summer engine and opencode for a 2-D console style RPG I’m working on. They both have strong suits and drawbacks.

I currently prefer opencode for system, rigging, and building out stuff I can tinker with in the IDE. Summer is better at prototype building and asset generation, but it seems to be geared more toward people who want to do minimal work inside the editor and do all development via prompt.

If I am comfortable getting my hands dirty and doing fine-tuning and polish myself, it seems like dropping my Summer Engine subscription and switching to OpenCode Go is a better use of similar expense, but I’m curious what others who may have tried both workflows have found.

comments.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
comments.body: While not plugged in for AI my engine is drag and drop and has everything you need for a 2D roof. Customizable and easier than rpg maker (which is what I played with). Built it because rpg maker was frustrating me with simple customization options

replies.author: LiveCourage334
replies.body: Interesting. I know it seems counterintuitive since I am asking about using AI as part of development, but I do want a more robust development environment. Part of my reasoning for this is to take some of the AI product management I use at work at leverage it for something personal.

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: I’m adding the option to plug in to any model, there’s an AI that can guide you and anything else you run into that’s confusing feel free to ask me and I’ll either direct you or update the engine to make that particular part easier.

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: The platform also has a few click publishing tool, a promotion kit that can be downloaded with one button and puts together and styles anything you put on that games page, a bug and Playtest key manager and some other things I’m still double checking before turning on

replies.author: LiveCourage334
replies.body: Yeah, I checked it out after your initial post. It kind of reminds me of Gdevelop. I’ve published a couple smaller projects through that engine and I really like it, but not what I’m looking for right now.

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: No worries, good luck with your game regardless!
